subject: how to write genetic distance values between genotypes to csv file in mat using POPPr package in R ?

messages.author: 404421b243bc9a2b
messages.subject: how to write genetic distance values between genotypes to csv file in mat using POPPr package in R ?
parts:
I calculated genetic distance based on SNP genotype data for my genotypes using provesti distance using bitewise function. I used this following code for this

snpsdist<-bitwise.dist(snps) save(snpsdist, ascii=TRUE, file="GPdist.CSV")

I want my distance values like below format but I failed to do so

         A     B      C    
A       0
B       0.34   0
C       0.39   0.45   0
Here I attached file containing my results in 1st sheet and how I wish to have in 2nd sheet.
can any one help me to write my results as above format? any help in this regard would be highly appreciated, sorry if I am not following any coding standards in this post Thanks and regard
Genetist

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: how to write genetic distance values between genotypes to csv file in mat using POPPr package in R ?
parts:
Hi Genetist,

There are two ways to get what you want, depending on what you want, exactly. 

If you want a lower triangle distance matrix, you can use the sink() function like so:

snpsdist <- bitwise.dist(snps)
sink(file = "GPdist.txt") # open the file
snpsdist # print output to file
sink() # close the file


There is also another way posted here: http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/Write-lower-half-of-distance-matrix-only-td863971.html

If what you really want is a symmetrical square matrix, then you should convert it to a matrix and use write.table:

snpsdist <- bitwise.dist(snps)
write.table(as.matrix(snpsdist), file = "GPdist.csv", rownames = TRUE, colnames = NA, sep = ",")

The reason why your previous approach didn't work is because the save() function is a bit misleading as it saves data in a way R can understand, but not in a way that is useful outside of R. 

Hope that helps!
Zhian
